criteria.criterion: AC1 — When the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the sha a gate pins, the gate emits ONE warning naming the build sha, the build commit's date, the pinned sha, and the drift count in commits. It does NOT fail and does NOT alter the verdict, exit code, signature, or provenance stamp.
AC2 — The warning is emitted at most once per (build sha, pinned sha) pair per process, so a run that resolves the handle more than once does not produce a warning storm.

AC3 — When build provenance is unavailable or drift cannot be established, the gate is SILENT: no warning when _gate_commit_sha() returns None, when the build sha is not present in the target repo, when the pinned sha is unknown, when git is unavailable, or when the build is at or ahead of the pinned sha.

AC4 — An unknown key in a config snapshot is reported differently when the running build is known to be behind the pinned ref: 'unknown key X (this build may predate it; see docs/config.md)' instead of the 'typo?' wording.

AC5 — Held-out unit tests cover: behind -> warns once; at/ahead -> silent; provenance unavailable -> silent; build sha absent from the target repo -> silent; and the config unknown-key wording in both the drifted and undrifted states.
